title: Water Wars
summary: Sources, methodology, AI disclosure and reusable animation tools for the Buried Signals Water Wars video. Material corrections and technical caveats are recorded below.

sources.claim: Early reporting estimated the project at up to 1 trillion yuan, about US$137 billion. At the July 2025 groundbreaking, China announced a higher estimate of 1.2 trillion yuan, about US$167.8 billion.
sources.title: State Council of China — Yarlung Zangbo project groundbreaking
sources.meta: Primary announcement · Updated official estimate · 19 Jul 2025

sources.claim: Before construction began, published estimates placed the project at up to 1 trillion yuan, approximately US$137 billion.
sources.title: The Economist — China approves the world's most expensive infrastructure project

sources.claim: The project is planned close to the India–China frontier, where the river falls nearly 2,000 metres; China has built hydropower projects upstream of India since work on Zangmu began in 2009.
sources.title: Made in China Journal — China's ambitions for the Lower Yarlung Tsangpo
sources.meta: Expert analysis · Location, hydropower history and project scale

sources.claim: Standard references put the Brahmaputra/Yarlung Tsangpo at roughly 2,850–2,900 kilometres, or about 1,800 miles.
sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica — Brahmaputra River

sources.claim: Banglapedia independently gives a source-to-mouth length of approximately 2,850 kilometres.
sources.title: Banglapedia — Brahmaputra River
sources.meta: National reference source · Corroborates river length

sources.claim: Reporting supports a major tunnel-diversion scheme through the Great Bend. Detailed final engineering plans are not public, and earlier reports described multiple 20-kilometre tunnels.
sources.title: BBC — China begins building world's largest dam

sources.claim: The projected 300 TWh annual output is equivalent to about 94% of the UK's 2024 electricity demand—reasonable scale shorthand for powering Britain for roughly a year.
sources.title: UK Government — DUKES 2025, Chapter 5: Electricity

sources.claim: About 97 million basin-dependent people are estimated in India and Bangladesh alone; wider Brahmaputra basin estimates exceed 100 million.
sources.title: ICIMOD — Brahmaputra key messages
sources.meta: Research synthesis · Supports rounded downstream scale

sources.claim: Arunachal Pradesh Chief Minister Pema Khandu called the project a 'water bomb' and an existential threat.
sources.title: The New Indian Express — Khandu calls project a ticking water bomb

sources.claim: Indian officials have warned of sudden-release risks and proposed the Upper Siang project as a buffer; China says downstream countries will not be harmed.
sources.title: Reuters — China's mega-dam triggers fears in India
sources.meta: Reuters reporting · Competing claims and project status

sources.claim: Thousands rallied along the Teesta demanding what organisers described as Bangladesh's fair share of the river's water.
sources.title: The Business Standard — Teesta protest march
sources.meta: Local reporting · Corroborated by Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha

sources.claim: The Indus system waters more than 90% of Pakistan's crops, while hydropower provides about one-fifth of its electricity.
sources.title: CSIS — Can India Cut Off Pakistan's Indus River Lifeline?

sources.claim: On 23 April 2025 India announced that the Indus Waters Treaty would be held in abeyance with immediate effect.
sources.title: Ministry of External Affairs, India — Special briefing

sources.claim: The treaty was signed in 1960 and survived wars and repeated periods of tension before India's 2025 abeyance announcement.
sources.title: World Bank — Indus Waters Treaty fact sheet

sources.claim: Afghanistan's Ministry of Water and Energy announced Chinese investment interest in three named Kunar hydropower projects: Shal, Sagi and Sartaq.
sources.title: Khaama Press — Chinese firm to construct three Kunar dams
sources.meta: Local reporting on ministry announcement · 29 Jul 2024

sources.claim: The three announced Kunar projects could materially affect downstream Pakistan and have already prompted strong Pakistani concern.
sources.title: The Diplomat — The ripple effects of Afghanistan's dam plans

sources.claim: The project's eight-country event filter yields 196 unique South Asian incidents in 2020–2024 and 73 in 2024—not the 76 shown in the video chart.
sources.title: Pacific Institute — Water Conflict Chronology event list
sources.meta: Event-level dataset · Independently recalculated · Chart correction

sources.claim: Glacier mass loss in the Hindu Kush Himalaya has accelerated.
sources.title: ICIMOD — Hindu Kush Himalaya glacier-loss findings

sources.claim: Wolf and colleagues found that dispute risk rises when rapid basin change exceeds institutional capacity; treaties are a central form of that capacity. The video applies this framework to the Indus treaty's disappearance as the final institutional break.
sources.title: Wolf et al. — Conflict and Cooperation Within International River Basins
sources.meta: Original research · Treaty and conflict-risk framework

sources.claim: The RFA-branded footage shows Indian and Chinese troops clashing along their disputed border. RFA says the exact filming date is uncertain.
sources.title: Radio Free Asia — Chinese, Indian soldiers skirmish along disputed border
sources.meta: Original publisher · Footage verified · Updated 15 Dec 2022

sources.claim: The Kashmir dispute dates to 1947; China controls Aksai Chin, which India claims, and the Indus crosses the wider historical Kashmir region through Ladakh.
sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica — Kashmir
sources.meta: Reference source · Territorial and river context

sources.claim: The canyon comparison began with National Park Service Grand Canyon footage and used credited Yarlung Tsangpo and Namcha Barwa images as visual references.
sources.title: National Park Service — Grand Canyon b-roll
sources.meta: Richard Burton / National Park Service · Public domain

sources.claim: A photograph of the narrow Yarlung Tsangpo gorge supplied river, rock-wall and scale references for the generated comparison.
sources.title: Wikimedia Commons — Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon

sources.claim: A Namcha Barwa photograph supplied the high-relief mountain reference for the canyon sequence.
sources.title: Wikimedia Commons — Namcha Barwa from the west

sources.claim: The Imja Glacier animation begins from a real archival photograph taken by Erwin Schneider between 1956 and 1961.
sources.title: Wikimedia Commons — Imja Glacier archival photograph

models: Krea and ComfyUI/Comfy Cloud were used to prototype and run Seedance 2.0 workflows for the Grand Canyon-to-Yarlung Tsangpo comparison.

ComfyUI/Comfy Cloud and Seedance 2.0 were used for glacier animations beginning from real archival photographs of Imja Glacier and Kyetrak/Gyarag Glacier. The generated endings are illustrative contemporary interpretations, not documentary photographs.
OpenAI Codex and other AI coding assistants supported Remotion development, source discovery, claim comparison and evidence organisation.
notAi: Source documents, published statistics, geodata and conflict-event data; AI output was not treated as evidence.
Reporting, narration, source selection, verification, editorial framing and publication decisions.

methodology.heading: Research
methodology.text: Reporting began with the script and source material. SearXNG was used for discovery and Crawl4AI to retrieve and preserve source pages. Primary records, original research and independent reporting were preferred.

methodology.heading: Verification
methodology.text: Claims were separated into testable assertions and checked with SIFT: investigate the source, find better coverage, trace it to origin and search for contradictions. The Pacific Institute data was recalculated from the underlying records, producing 196 unique incidents for 2020–2024 and 73 in 2024.

methodology.heading: Visuals
methodology.text: Maps and charts were built in Remotion from documented data and GeoJSON. MapTiler supplied satellite and vector basemaps, terrain and contextual country borders; explicit disputed boundaries and river routes used Natural Earth, OpenStreetMap and project-curated geometry. AI-assisted canyon and glacier sequences are disclosed separately.
